name: 1password-developer-environments
description: Manage 1Password Developer Environments from Claude on macOS. Set up, mount, and inspect project secrets and .env files without exposing values.
long_description:
Connects Claude to the 1Password desktop app's local MCP server for [1Password Developer Environments](https://www.1password.dev/).

The extension lets Claude help with secure project environment setup — listing Developer Environments, inspecting variable names, adding variables, and creating local `.env` mounts. Secret values stay controlled by the 1Password desktop app and are never shared with Claude.

**Platform:** macOS only. The MCP server binary ships with the 1Password desktop app and runs locally; nothing is sent to a remote 1Password service by this extension.

**Prerequisites:**

- macOS with the 1Password desktop app installed.
- The **1Password Labs MCP Server** experiment enabled in the desktop app (`onepassword://settings/labs`).
- A 1Password account with Developer Environments enabled.

tools.name: authenticate
tools.description: Authenticate with the 1Password desktop app and return the accountId. Call this first in a turn unless you already have an accountId. The desktop app may prompt the user for approval on first connection.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: List Developer Environments for an account. Requires accountId.

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Create a new Developer Environment. Requires accountId and a name.

tools.name: rename_environment
tools.description: Rename an existing Developer Environment. Requires accountId and environmentId.

tools.name: list_variables
tools.description: List variable names in an Environment without returning their values. Requires accountId and environmentId. Summarize names only — never request or display values.

tools.name: append_variables
tools.description: Add or update Environment variables. Requires accountId and environmentId. Mark secret values as concealed; use concealed:false only for non-sensitive values such as URLs or feature flags. Ask the user before creating or modifying variables unless the request is already explicit.

tools.name: create_local_env_file
tools.description: Mount an Environment as a local .env file. Requires accountId, environmentId, environmentName, and an absolute mountPath. macOS only. Do not read the mounted file to verify it — use list_local_env_files instead.

tools.name: list_local_env_files
tools.description: List existing local .env mounts for an Environment. Requires accountId and environmentId.

prompts.name: mount-env
prompts.description: Mount a 1Password Developer Environment as this project's local .env file.
prompts.text:
Mount the 1Password Developer Environment "${arguments.environment}" as a local .env file in the current project.

Steps:
1. Call authenticate and store the accountId. The 1Password desktop app may prompt for approval.
2. Call list_environments to resolve "${arguments.environment}" to an environmentId. If the name is ambiguous, ask me to choose — do not guess.
3. Call list_local_env_files to check for an existing mount at the target path.
4. Derive the absolute mountPath by appending /.env to the current workspace root.
5. If no duplicate exists, call create_local_env_file with accountId, environmentId, environmentName, and the absolute mountPath.
6. Report the mount path and Environment name. Do not read the mounted .env file to verify it.

prompts.name: list-environments
prompts.text: List my 1Password Developer Environments. Call authenticate first to obtain an accountId (the desktop app may prompt for approval), then call list_environments and summarize the results.

prompts.name: inspect-variables
prompts.description: Show the variable names in a 1Password Developer Environment without revealing values.
prompts.text:
Show the variable names in the 1Password Developer Environment "${arguments.environment}".

1. Call authenticate and store the accountId.
2. Call list_environments and resolve "${arguments.environment}" to an environmentId, asking me to choose if it is ambiguous.
3. Call list_variables and summarize the returned variable names only. Do not request or display any secret values.
